_comment: Tuned NB roadster: the 1999 body (same model and cabin as nb1999) on the 2004 factory turbo car's drivetrain, brakes, bars and 17 in wheel and tyre size (Mazda 2004 MAZDASPEED MX-5 specification sheet), with aftermarket coilovers (Flyin' Miata V-Maxx XXtreme Sport rates), a street alignment, a generic 17 x 7 ten-spoke wheel and a small deck-lid lip spoiler. Calibrated against the 2004 factory turbo car's instrumented tests; the coilovers are the one change from that car (see sources.coilovers). Every value not published is listed in sources.estimates.
name: 1999 Roadster Turbo, tuned

sources.factory_turbo_car: Mazda North American Operations, 2004 MAZDASPEED MX-5 Miata technical specifications (https://news.mazdausa.com/download/04-MS-MX-5-Miata-Spec-Sheet.pdf): 178 hp SAE net at 6000 rpm, 166 lb-ft (225 N·m) at 4500 rpm, 6500 rpm redline, 8.5 psi maximum boost, IHI turbocharger and air-to-air intercooler, 9.5:1 compression; six-speed 3.76/2.27/1.65/1.26/1.00/0.84, 4.10 final drive; 2529 lb (1147 kg) with 52:48 weight distribution; 89.2 in wheelbase, 55.7/56.7 in track; springs 37.7/27.6 N/mm, bars 23/14 mm, Bilstein dampers; 17 x 7 wheels, 205/40R17 tyres; 10.6 in vented front and 10.9 in solid rear discs with four-wheel ABS; 2.3 turns lock to lock, 34.2 ft turning circle.
sources.calibration: 0-60 mph: MotorWeek 7.1 s (https://motorweek.org/road_tests/2004_mazdaspeed_mx5_miata_program_2404/) and Car and Driver 6.7 s (as listed by https://www.0-60specs.com/mazda/mx-5-miata-0-60-times); the target 6.9 s with a 0.25 s band covers both. 60-0 mph: MotorWeek 113 ft; a forum transcription of Sport Compact Car gives 114 ft (https://mazdas247.com/forum/threads/msp-vs-msm.47621/page-3), so 113.5 ft. Skidpad: 0.90 g, Car and Driver as quoted on owner forums (the same thread; AnandTech forum quotes 0.91 g, https://forums.anandtech.com/threads/follow-up-test-2004-mazdaspeed-miata-mx-5.1285772/post-10862995). The skidpad figure is low confidence: no primary copy of the test was reachable.
sources.turbo: Boost builds from about 2500 rpm and is full by 3500 rpm: Drivingline, the turbo 'takes over at 3,500 rpm' (https://www.drivingline.com/articles/looking-back-driving-a-bone-stock-2004-mazdaspeed-mx-5-miata/); MotorWeek describes a strong pull from 4500 rpm with no noticeable lag; Motor Illustrated calls it lag-laden with a narrow powerband (https://motorillustrated.com/2004-mazda-mx-5-miata-mazdaspeed-review/8485/). No boost-versus-rpm log is published.
sources.torque_curves: Full boost: only 225 N·m at 4500 rpm and 211 N·m at 6000 rpm (178 hp) are published; the points between and below are an estimate shaped like a small single-scroll turbo's plateau. Off boost (torque_curve): the 1999 engine's curve (nb1999.json) times 0.95 for the lower compression and the turbine's back-pressure, an estimate.
sources.coilovers: Flyin' Miata V-Maxx XXtreme, NB Sport package: 391 lb/in front, 258 lb/in rear (https://www.flyinmiata.com/products/fm-v-maxx-xxtreme-coilovers-sport-package-nb; Moss Miata listing https://mossmiata.com/910-776-mcc-cp-vmaxx-stage-2-coilover-packages-by-flyin-miata). Deviation from the factory turbo car: its springs are 37.7/27.6 N/mm (215/158 lb/in) on Bilstein dampers and it sits 7 mm under the standard car (MotorWeek); this car has the stiffer coilover springs (wheel rates 31.7/26.8 kN/m, ride frequencies about 1.7 Hz against 1.2 Hz), sits 25 mm under the standard car, and keeps the factory 23/14 mm bars. Why: the user asked for coilovers; the V-Maxx Sport rates are the published street coilover for the NB, and the factory bars balance it. The calibration skidpad was also run with the factory springs, ride height and alignment (docs/cars.md).
sources.ride_height: 25 mm under the standard NB (mount_height_m 0.51 + 0.010 for the larger tyre + 0.025). Flyin' Miata recommends about 11.5-12 in front and 12-12.5 in rear fender height with these coilovers, roughly an inch under stock; the stock fender height is not published, so the 25 mm is an estimate.
sources.alignment: Flyin' Miata street/performance recommendation (https://help.flyinmiata.com/en_us/align-your-suspension-chakras-By4oIc2zj.md): caster 5.0°, camber -1.0° front and -1.5° rear, toe-in 1/16 in total (about 0.075° per wheel) front and rear.
sources.steering: Lock 31.8° derived from the 34.2 ft turning circle against the standard car's 30.2 ft at 36.6°; ratio 13.0:1 derived from 2.3 turns lock to lock over that lock (Mazda sheet). Steering stiffness and pneumatic trail as CarSpec.gd.
sources.wheels_tyres: 17 x 7, offset +40 (one used-parts listing of the factory wheel, https://importapart.com/products/327078279116), 205/40R17. Wheel mass about 8.5 kg and tyre about 9 kg are estimates (a 205/40R17 Kumho V700 weighed 19.2 lb, https://mazdas247.com/forum/t/msp-racing-hart-weight.26085; Toyo R888R 205/40R17 21 lb, https://tiresize.com/tires/Toyo/Proxes-R888R-205-40R17.htm). The rim drawn in the game is a generic ten-spoke, not the factory design.
sources.spoiler: A small deck-lid lip, as on the factory turbo car. No lift or downforce figure exists for any NB spoiler; a few centimetres of lip makes a few kilograms at most at 60 mph (estimate), so it is visual only and drag_area_m2 is unchanged.
sources.estimates: Inertia (the 1999 car's scaled by mass), centre of gravity height relative to the body (unchanged, so it drops with the body), off-boost torque curve and the full-boost points between the published two, spool time 0.4 s, bypass-valve vent 0.15 s, clutch capacity 290 N·m, wheel inertia 1.23 kg·m² (the 1999 car's 1.05 plus the heavier 17 in wheel and tyre), unsprung mass 24 kg, damping ratios (the V-Maxx XXtreme is adjustable; mid setting assumed), reverse ratio (the five-speed's), ride height, steering stiffness, tyre grip (calibrated to the tests above).
